items.title: In the biotech world, you can’t see everything
items.raw_text: Earlier this week, I attended a screening of You Can See Everything , the buzzy new documentary about the disgraced former biotech CEO Elizabeth Holmes. I went in not really knowing what to expect. I’d avoided spoilers (and won’t be giving anything away here, either!). I was wondering what new information this film could reveal, given how familiar many of us are with the Theranos story thanks to years of media coverage, the best-selling book Bad Blood , and the Hulu series The Dropout , starring Amanda Seyfried. Like many others who have seen the film, I came away feeling unsettled. But not just about Holmes’s fraud and the somewhat disturbing interactions between the subjects. The film reignited a concern I’ve had about covering science for most of my career: Despite our best efforts, we never can actually see everything . She went on to claim that her company had invented a way to run over 100 diagnostic tests on just a few drops of blood. items.title: Designing an AI serving harness built to last
items.raw_text: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it. That’s an important shift. For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context windows, higher benchmark scores. Those advances have been extraordinary. But as AI moves from experimentation to production, the question facing enterprise leaders has changed—it’s no longer, “what can the model do?”—it’s now, “Can we deliver that intelligence reliably, economically, and at scale?” Increasingly, the answer depends on the serving harness—the engineering system surrounding the model, including the architecture, memory management , scheduling, and optimization decisions that determine how efficiently model intelligence becomes a production capability. For technical executives, that changes where AI investment should go—and what they should demand from the architecture supporting it. Start with the workload, not the model There is no universally “best” model or AI architecture. There is only the right solution for the business problem. The Three-Layer Cake: Public-Interest Information in an AI-Intermediated Age draws on a year of convenings and conversations with journalists, technologists, funders, investors, and other experts. It considers how journalism must evolve as AI systems increasingly stand between information providers and the people they serve. [Clip] The report outlines three connected layers: the products that identify what people want to know, the systems that synthesize answers, and the organizations that produce the underlying reporting. Each layer, the report argues, requires attention and distinct strategies to serve the public interest. The report identifies several priorities for collective action, including shared standards that allow sourcing, context, and other essential information to travel with individual facts as AI systems use them. It also calls for greater visibility into how those systems select information and frame answers. items.raw_text: Enterprise AI can generate recommendations, automate tasks, and help organizations make decisions faster. But without an understanding of how a business actually operates, even powerful models can miss the constraints and relationships that determine whether a decision is the right one. As companies look to move AI from experimentation into everyday operations, the challenge ahead is giving technology the context to act usefully within complex business processes. For Devavrat Shah, chief scientist of enterprise AI at Celonis, that context is central to what he calls “decision intelligence.” AI agents can support individual tasks within larger decision-making processes, he argues, but they need to understand the role each task plays and the business conditions surrounding it. “You can’t just do that in a vacuum,” he says. Without the right operational context, agents risk overlooking important constraints, making costly mistakes, or consuming excessive computing resources as they try to work out what they need to know. The solution begins with connecting AI to the processes and data enterprises already use. A contextual layer can help agents understand workflows, operate within defined guardrails, and produce recommendations that people can review and approve. items.raw_text: How much do you know about permafrost? Maybe, like me, you’ve been aware that this layer of frozen soil is thawing, that it’s important in the global puzzle of climate change … and that’s about the extent of it. The great news for both of us is that my colleague James Temple just published two in-depth stories about permafrost. His reporting took him to the boreal forests of Alaska, where he helicoptered into the wilderness to learn more about how this material could affect our climate both now and in the future. I’d recommend you give both of James’s stories a read. There’s this feature about efforts to tackle the intensifying fires that are threatening permafrost, as well as this look at how researchers are trying to understand the complicated tangle of potential climate effects. Here are three things I took away. Permafrost is a massive blind spot for climate change Permafrost is the frozen layer of soil that’s under about 15% of land around the Northern Hemisphere. While technically material needs to be frozen for only two consecutive years to count as permafrost, most of our current permafrost formed during the last ice age. That means there’s organic material that’s been frozen, and essentially locked away, for thousands of years. Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
items.raw_text: A security researcher has demonstrated a software-only partial jailbreak of the Switch 2, gaining "userland" access that he says "lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO." The hack relies on the original Switch version of SmileBasic 4 , the latest in a long-running series of programming environments and interpreters that run on Nintendo hardware. The so-called "tethered" hack also requires access to a macOS or Linux PC on the same network to run a node.js package that helps enable privileged system access. Researcher Sammy Hajhamid writes that he used OpenAI's Codex to poke at SmileBasic's language interpreter, using a custom harness that could send USB commands to the system and view results via HDMI (as well as power cycling via a Bluetooth light switch flipping device). After "substantial effort for ~2 weeks," that harness discovered a 32-bit integer overflow that occurs when removing items from an array in SmileBasic. That error gives access to an array pointer, which in turn allows read and write access to portions of system memory. Read full article Comments

items.title: Ink droplets in motion snag top prize in Nikon Small World contest
items.raw_text: A 25-year-old German experimental photographer has won the 2026 Nikon Small World photomicrography competition with a striking image of droplets of ink being deposited on paper by an inkjet printer. Ole Bielfeldt beat out 1,802 other entries hailing from 69 different countries. Bielfeldt became interested in photomicrography during the COVID-19 lockdown after discovering an old microscope in his parents' attic. He figured out how to build an adaptor out of a tube and some wood to connect the microscope to his father's camera and taught himself the art through trial and error, building custom tools as needed. He documents how he captures transformative images of everyday objects with behind-the-scenes videos posted to macrofying , his photography and videography brand. It was Bielfeldt's curiosity about the inner workings of inkjet printers that inspired his winning entry, but capturing the action of ink drops being deposited on paper was a challenge, given that the process happens so quickly. The droplets, for instance, moved faster than the camera's shutter speed. Bielfeldt's solution was to deconstruct the printer so that the paper moved under a stationary (rather than moving) printhead, and then take the image in a dark room, using a flash to serve as the shutter, thereby freezing the ink drops mid-air. There was no need for pricey equipment. Bielfeldt does not use AI in his images, preferring to rely on traditional techniques. Read full article Comments

This emulator reimagines Nintendo’s Virtual Boy with a full color display
items.raw_text: Last year, we reported on Red Viper , a Virtual Boy emulator that added a splash of Super Game Boy-style color to Nintendo's famously failed red-on-black "portable" 3D headset from the '90s. Now, a new emulation experiment, VBoy Color , has taken the concept to a higher level, using a tile-based palette system that allows for many more distinct colors in each individual Virtual Boy frame. Rather than simply replacing the Virtual Boy's four shades of red with four different colors, VBoy Color's readme files explain how the emulator's game-specific Color Packs can assign a distinct four-color palette to each 8x8 tile in a Virtual Boy scene. That means the emulator can differentiate between green pipes, grey platforms, and red brick wall in Mario Clash , for instance, even though all those in-game objects share the same overlapping red hues in the original game. The Game Boy Color-esque results feel like being transported into an alternate history where Nintendo invested in a full-color display rather than cheaper red LEDs for the Virtual Boy hardware. The increased contrast between differently colored elements is particularly welcome in games like Jack Bros. or Vertical Force , where the original red-on-red display often makes it hard to differentiate the player-character from busy red background elements. De geselecteerde incubator zal een Venture Incubation Programme (VIP) verzorgen voor early-stage Europese startups die werken met Large Language Models (LLMs) en generatieve AI. Het programma start in juni 2027 en richt zich op het begeleiden van startups bij marktvalidatie, het aanscherpen van businessmodellen en voorbereiding op opschaling. Daarnaast is er nadruk op grensoverschrijdende samenwerking, kennisdeling en de ontwikkeling van verantwoordelijke AI-oplossingen die aansluiten bij Europa’s taalkundige en culturele diversiteit. Aanmelden en meer informatie De deadline om aan te melden is 23 maart 2027 (17:00 CET) . Aanmelden? De call staat op de website van LLM-BRIDGE. De geselecteerde incubator verzorgt een gestructureerd incubatieprogramma van twaalf weken. Binnen het LLM-BRIDGE-project is hiervoor ondersteuning beschikbaar via het Europese FSTP-mechanisme. Alle details over voorwaarden en de aanmeldprocedure zijn te vinden op de website van LLM Bridge . Over LLM-BRIDGE LLM-BRIDGE is een Europees initiatief dat zich richt op het versterken van het GenAI-ecosysteem. Het project ondersteunt startups, scale-ups, incubators en investeerders bij het ontwikkelen en toepassen van betrouwbare, meertalige AI-oplossingen en bestaat uit drie samenhangende programma’s voor de LLM- en GenAI-sector.

items.title: Podcast De Dag: de kwetsbaarheid van PHP, 'de onderbroek' van het internet
items.raw_text: Van DigiD tot de Franse overheid, en van RTL Nieuws tot Schiphol. Sites van allerlei instanties gingen gisteren een paar uur offline. Er zaten lekken in PHP, een taal om sites te programmeren. Doordat die lekken op straat lagen, waren de sites kwetsbaar voor hackers. En dus was het veiliger om websites even uit de lucht te halen. Wat zegt dit lek over de kwetsbaarheid van ons internet? Luister hier: Deze aflevering van De Dag luister je via NPO Luister en alle andere podcastapps. Bevalt het? Vergeet je dan niet te abonneren. Volgens techjournalist van de NOS Joost Schellevis kan je PHP vergelijken met een onderbroek. Iedereen gebruikt het, het is belangrijk, maar normaal blijft het onzichtbaar. Met behulp van AI is het lek in die onderbroek nu gevonden. Kunstmatige intelligentie is een vloek en zegen voor de kwetsbaarheid van het internet. Aan de ene kant worden meer lekken gedicht die een mens moeilijk kan vinden. Aan de andere kant kunnen hackers die kwaad in de zin hebben, makkelijker toeslaan. Ook techsite Tweakers ging offline. Dat was jammer, want juist daar wilden ze over dit lek schrijven. Normaal gesproken wordt er pas over geschreven als de oplossing, een patch, voorhanden is. Maar nu ging die volgorde overhoop, waardoor het halve internet op zwart ging. Tweakers-hoofdredacteur Wout Funnekotter vreest dat dit niet de laatste keer zal zijn. items.title: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email
items.raw_text: Unknown hackers hijacked more than 300 Tor exit nodes and reconfigured them to favor unencrypted email traffic and redirect SSH connections through servers they controlled, a researcher reported Tuesday. The hijacking began in late August, when, according to Tor volunteers , the attacker used a valid password that had been reused to gain access to a Tor management server. The attacker then installed Ebury , a backdoor written for Linux that was discovered 12 years ago. Mysteries remain Then the attacker connected from the management server to a second Tor server, called Switzerland2, through SSH, using an RSA key that, for unknown reasons, investigators couldn’t find among Switzerland2’s authorized keys. With administrative control of Switzerland2, the attackers installed Ebury there as well. Finally, the attacker reconfigured settings on two exit nodes that Switzerland2 hosted. items.title: UN says we're going to blow past 1.5º warming, offers a "now what?" answer
items.raw_text: In 2015, all but two countries agreed to make an effort to keep global temperatures from reaching 1.5° C above pre-industrial readings. Since then, most of the world has largely treated what they signed on to as aspirational, and one of the largest emitters (the US) has alternately withdrawn and recommitted to the agreement. Meanwhile, the planet has responded as expected to steadily rising carbon emissions and appears to be practically at the 1.5° limit. On Wednesday, for the first time, the United Nations Environmental Programme (UNEP) acknowledged that reality and conceded that the goal of keeping warming below 1.5° was no longer a viable one. Instead, its new goalposts focus on keeping both how long we exceed that limit and how much we exceed it by, at a minimum. Doing that will require both dramatic emissions cuts now and the removal of hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere before the century is out. Bowing to the inevitable Depending on which baseline you use to establish pre-industrial temperatures, as well as which reconstruction of global temperatures you rely on, the world has either gotten very close to, or already exceeded, the 1.5° milestone. The current El Niño event, which appears exceptionally strong, will almost certainly mean that we've gone over it no matter which records you choose. Read full article Comments

items.raw_text: Demand for new PCs took a hit after months of price hikes, with Counterpoint Research reporting global PC shipments fell 21 percent year-over-year in Q3 2026. items.title: Waarom het Nederlandse bedrijfsleven cloudinfrastructuur met soevereiniteit nodig heeft
items.raw_text: Nederlandse organisaties behoren tot een van de meest digitaal geavanceerde economieën ter wereld. Van multinationals en financiële instellingen tot zorgorganisaties, maakbedrijven en scale-ups: vrijwel iedere sector is afhankelijk van cloudgebaseerde, datagedreven en AI-ondersteunde platformen om concurrerend en wendbaar te blijven. Die afhankelijkheid biedt kansen, maar brengt ook risico’s met zich mee. Naarmate bedrijfskritische processen, data en AI-modellen vaker in internationale cloudomgevingen worden ondergebracht, groeit de behoefte aan controle over gegevens, systemen en besluitvorming. Dat raakt direct aan compliance, cybersecurity, bedrijfscontinuïteit en strategische autonomie. Tegelijkertijd stelt Europese regelgeving, zoals de AVG, NIS2 en DORA, steeds hogere eisen aan gegevensbescherming, cyberweerbaarheid en operationele veerkracht. Organisaties moeten aantoonbaar grip hebben op opslag, verwerking, toegang en governance. De centrale vraag is daarom hoe bedrijven de voordelen van cloud en AI kunnen benutten zonder controle over kritieke data, intellectueel eigendom en strategische besluitvorming te verliezen. Indurex haalt 7 miljoen euro op voor beveiliging van industriële systemen Het Amsterdamse bedrijf Indurex heeft een investeringsronde van zeven miljoen euro afgerond. De financiering werd geleid door Contrarian Ventures, met deelname van Axeleo Capital en Curiosity. Indurex ontwikkelt een platform dat ai inzet voor de beveiliging van industriële systemen in onder meer de energie-, industrie-, utiliteits- en datacentermarkt. Het bedrijf richt zich op de combinatie van operationele technologie (ot), engineeringgegevens en cybersecurity om afwijkingen en risico’s in industriële omgevingen sneller te signaleren. Volgens Indurex wordt het kapitaal gebruikt voor onderzoek en ontwikkeling en voor commerciële uitbreiding in, in eerste instantie, Europa en het Midden-Oosten. Lantack levert beheerde ict-diensten en is gespecialiseerd in Microsoft 365, Azure en Modern Workplace-oplossingen. Het bedrijf werd in 2008 opgericht door Cliff Lagendijk en telt tien medewerkers.
